description: Reads an image with a moving read head and turns the colour under it into voltages, gates and triggers

params.text: Limits how fast the v output can move; at 0% it is not limited at all, and higher settings slow it down
Switches between Unipolar, where the v output runs 0-10V and x and y are measured from the top left corner of the image, and Bipolar, where x and y are measured from the centre
Starts and stops the read head
Chooses how the read head moves over the image: Scanline, Bounce, Vinyl, Wander, X/Y Pad, Tabalar or Ralabat; the chosen one is named in the lit display in the middle of the panel
Sets how fast the read head moves, 0 to 100, before the multiplier is applied
Multiplies the speed setting by a whole number from x1 to x10
Chooses which part of the colour under the read head feeds the v, g and t outputs: Lightness, Luminance, Saturation, Hue, Minimum, Maximum, Average, Red, Green, Blue or Alpha
Sets how far the last six readings of the chosen colour part have to spread before a trigger fires, 0 to 1 against readings that run 0-10V, so a low setting fires often
Sets the shortest time between one trigger and the next, 0 to 1000ms

inputs.text: A trigger here switches the read head between playing and paused
A trigger here puts the read head back at its saved start position
Sets the horizontal position of the read head, 0-10V across the width of the image; the read head follows the cables only while this jack and the one beside it are both patched
Sets the vertical position of the read head, 0-10V down the height of the image; with both position jacks patched the path, speed and multiplier settings are not used
Sets the speed knob from a cable, 0-10V covering its 0 to 100 range; the voltage is written into the knob, so the knob moves, and the jack is not read while both position jacks are patched
Adds to the minimum trigger time, 50ms per volt on top of the knob setting

outputs.text: The horizontal position of the read head, 0-10V across the width of the image, or measured from the middle of the image with the polarity switch on Bipolar
The vertical position of the read head, 0-10V down the height of the image, or measured from the middle of the image and rising upwards with the polarity switch on Bipolar

The chosen part of the colour under the read head, 0-10V, limited in speed by the slew knob; with the polarity switch on Bipolar it is that same voltage less 0.5V, not the -5V to +5V the manual states
Flips between 0V and 10V each time a trigger fires, once six readings have been taken
A 10V pulse each time the spread of the last six readings passes the g/t setting and the minimum time has gone by
The red part of the colour under the read head, 0-10V
The green part of the colour under the read head, 0-10V
The blue part of the colour under the read head, 0-10V

notes: the module reads nothing until an image is loaded: click the picture button to open one, or drag an image file onto the image area
shift-click the picture button to reload the file, and Cmd+Shift-click on Mac or Ctrl+Shift-click elsewhere to close it
click the image to put the read head where you clicked, and drag to scrub, whichever path is chosen
with the path set to X/Y Pad and no image loaded, the module is a plain XY pad, and the x and y outputs follow the polarity switch
the v, g, t, R, G and B outputs are worked out only while at least one of those six has a cable in it; with none patched, the read head moves but no colour is computed
the small round button beside the r jack returns the read head to its start position, and shift-clicking it makes the present position the new start; no click on it reaches this help
the picture button opening the image file is not a parameter either, so no click on it reaches this help
every knob is also a click control: click to step the value up, Cmd-click on Mac or Ctrl-click elsewhere to step down, and hold Shift for ten times the step
with the colour part set to Alpha, an image with no transparency gives a steady maximum voltage
menu: Labels — shows or hides the lettering printed beside the knobs and jacks
Gold medallion — shows or hides the gold #d mark
Bright image in a dark room — the image is not dimmed when the Rack room brightness is turned down
